questions.q: A scaling intent is raised when the composite load score:
options: Exceeds 0.5 for a single window
Dips below 0.25
Exceeds 0.75 for three consecutive five-minute evaluation windows
Changes by more than 10% between scrapes
questions.explain: The window evaluator distinguishes spikes (connection pool adjustments) from sustained trends (compute scaling): a single window breach only resets the cooldown and increases monitoring frequency.

questions.q: Why is the cooldown mechanism (30-minute default) described as non-negotiable in the vertical scaling controller?
options: Without it, resize-induced latency looks like continued stress and triggers a feedback loop scaling to the maximum SKU
Cloud APIs require a 30-minute gap between calls
It gives engineers time to read the alert
It is mandated by PCI compliance
questions.explain: Scaling up briefly increases latency during the resize; without a cooldown, the controller reads its own disruption as continued stress and scales again, looping to the ceiling SKU.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the chapter's hard scale-down guardrails?
options: Minimum replica floor (2 for single-AZ, 1 for Multi-AZ)
Replication lag gate against the SLA
Active backup exclusion
Time-of-day window — scale-down only on weekends
questions.explain: The four hard guardrails are the replica floor, the replication lag gate, active backup exclusion, and the 60-minute post-failover observation window — none of them is a calendar window, and only a human operator can override them.

questions.q: The predictive scaling layer trains a Prophet model on how much composite-signal history, and looks ahead how far?
options: 7 days of history, 1-hour lookahead
30 days of history, 4-hour lookahead
90 days of history, 24-hour lookahead
12 hours of history, 15-minute lookahead
questions.explain: The predictive controller loads 30 days of composite score history on a 15-minute cron and generates a 4-hour forecast, producing a preemptive scale-up intent when a peak above 0.75 is predicted.

questions.q: When a scaling intent is blocked by the cost guardrail, what happens?
options: The intent is silently dropped
The system retries every minute until approved
The controller raises a COST_GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED alert with resource ID, blocked target SKU, projected overspend, and remaining budget so a human judges the cost-performance trade-off
The monthly budget cap is automatically raised
questions.explain: Blocked intents are surfaced as explicit operational alerts with full context; the system neither silently overspends nor silently degrades, and a human makes the trade-off call.
